These are all the powerful, encounter-changing potion passives obtainable via Distillation.
When you click **Distill Elixir**, three are randomly offered as the 'core' for the run. The reagents then tune its Duration Power and Value Power.

*You want to understand the process before committing? Sensible. Most don't bother. They poison themselves.*

Distillation combines the arcane and science to produce powerful potion passives. Choose your core wisely — it cannot be changed once the process begins.

**Step 1 — Choose a Core:**
Three passives are offered. Each shows its possible value and duration ranges. This is the passive you will receive. Everything after this point merely determines *how powerful* that passive becomes. Do not rush.

**Steps 2–9 — Reagent Selection:**
At each step, three reagents appear — each bearing a special property. Each step bears a dust cost: You cannot select what you cannot afford. After selection, your **Value Power** or **Duration Power** might change.

**Reagent Temperament:**
🟢 **Verdant** — measured, steady. Consistent gains or losses.
🔵 **Astral** — balanced. Neither spectacular nor catastrophic.
🔴 **Crimson** — volatile. Large swings either way.

Your primary job is `/combat`. Find a monster, fight it, survive. Every kill earns gold and experience, and as you grow stronger you'll find gear that can be enhanced with passives that change how you fight — weapons that chain hits, armor that shrugs off blows.

Learn what your equipment actually does. A warrior who doesn't know their own kit is just a liability with a sword.

Not everything worth having comes off a monster's corpse. `/gather`, to keep your tools up to date, you passively gather materials while you're away — ore from the deep, fish from cursed rivers, timber from whatever forest hasn't tried to kill someone this week.

The resources feed the crafting systems. Upgrading your tools makes the work faster. The best adventurers I've known idled smart, not hard.

The ideology you named isn't decoration — it's the mark you leave on this server. Spread it and others will follow. Or they'll oppose you, which is just as interesting.

*I'm not going to hold your hand through this. But I will make sure you leave this hall knowing what you're walking into.*

Combat is straightforward: your **Attack** determines how hard and how often you land hits; your **Defence** affects how hard it hits back. **Percent DR** and **Flat DR** reduce incoming damage further. Miss a hit and you deal nothing — accuracy matters. Land a **Critical Hit** and you deal bonus damage.

You carry **Potions**. Use them mid-fight to restore HP — but it costs you a turn, so pick your moment. If it's going badly, **Flee**. There's no shame in survival.

*Another adventurer just out of the woodwork? Come closer, let me inspect that pitiful frame of yours...*

Not bad. You'll do. Slayer is the art of killing not just monsters, but the right type of monster. I'll give you a species to hunt. Your job is to kill a specific number of them - you'll find your targets through regular combat. Complete the task and you earn **Slayer XP** and some favor with me.

Here, take this Emblem. It absorbs the very essence of the slayer monsters you kill, granting you boons or challenges to face.
As you become a master of slayer yourself, you'll unlock more slots. Fill them. You'll feel the difference.

*Oh, a new face! Don't be shy — I don't bite. Much.*

I keep a small but very important stock here. **Potions** are what keep you breathing out there — buy them before every fight. The cost goes up as you level, but so does how much they heal. Run out mid-combat and you'll regret it.

*Welcome adventurer! I'm Yuna, Master Tamer and keeper of the Companion Ranch.*

Companions are creatures that travel with you and **passively boost your stats**. Each has a passive type — ATK, DEF, Hit, Crit, Ward, Rarity, and more — and a tier that determines how strong the bonus is. Your **active companion(s)** are always working for you in combat.

Companions can be tamed through combat or rarely from boss encounters. You can even fuse two companions together!

Companions can gain levels via XP, and you gain companion XP from discarding unwanted equipment (more upgrades = more xp). The Companion Ranch down at the Settlement can also produce XP cookies to feed to your pets.

*Every great force needs a home. This is yours.*

Your Settlement is what makes this ideology real — it's a central base for that ideology's followers. **Logging Camps** and **Quarries** generate materials automatically. The **Nursery** produce followers. Assign staff, take Development Turns, and watch it compound.

**Zeal** is the fuel you earn from fighting and quests. Spend it to take a **Development Turn**, which advances construction, upgrades, and events. As your **Town Hall** tiers up, new building slots unlock — eventually you're working with a Black Market, War Camps, and Watchtowers that amplify everything around them. Oh, and ask Spritz if you're not sure what to do, she's over there.

*I'll be brief — you've got work to do.*

Every weapon and piece of armor I forge depends on what comes out of the ground, the forest, and the water. **Mining**, **Woodcutting**, and **Fishing** — that's where your supply chain starts.

Upgrade your **tools** when you can. Better tools reach better veins, richer timber, deeper water. The materials from higher-tier nodes are categorically different from what you pull with iron. Quantity matters, but quality matters more.

**Artisan Mastery** unlocks passive bonuses that compound over time — yield increases, rare material chances, synergy between skills. The more you invest in a skill, the more it pays back.

*Listen carefully. I've lost workers in those tunnels. I won't lose another because they skipped the briefing.*

The Delve is an expedition into unstable mining layers. Pay the permit fee and drill down. Every layer is a hazard — **Gas Pockets**, **Magma Flows**, **Gravel** — and each drains your **Stability**. Hit zero and the run collapses; you come out with nothing.

**Ore Veins** are what you're after. They yield rare Obsidian Shards you won't find anywhere else. You'll pick up regular ore along the way as well.

Three upgrades matter: **Fuel** (how deep you go), **Structure** (damage you absorb), and **Sensor** (preview the next layer before committing). Invest in all three.

*The guild attracts all kinds. Some of them are worth keeping close.*

Partners are NPC allies recruited with **Guild Tickets**. Set one as your active partner and they contribute **combat skills** in every fight — attack boosts, crit bonuses, survivability buffs. The skills they bring depend entirely on who you recruit, so read before you commit.

When combat isn't the priority, put one on **Dispatch** — timed missions that run in the background and return gold, materials, and keys while you're busy elsewhere. Dispatch accumulates for up to 48 hours. Check back when it makes sense.

Rarer partners carry stronger signature skills. The grind for them is real, but so is the return.

*You've wandered into my lab. How fortunate — for you.*

Alchemy is not mere potion-mixing. It is the art of coaxing power out of reluctant materials, and occasionally out of catastrophe.

My laboratory handles three disciplines:
**Transmutation** — shift your gathered resources up or down the tier ladder. Efficient. Reliable. Occasionally expensive, but that is the cost of ambition.
**Synthesis** — convert keys, essences, and other materials into Cosmic Dust, or use Dust to produce something more immediately useful. The process is straightforward.
**The Potion Lab** — my masterwork. Use *Distill Elixir* to run a distillation experiment that imprints a powerful passive onto your potions.

Level up to unlock additional potion passive slots. You may one day have as many as five active.

*I don't hand out rewards for nothing. But I do hand them out.*

The board runs two tracks. **Daily Contracts** are short-term — kill X, deal Y damage, clear a boss. Finish them and you earn **Quest Tokens**, which you spend in the shop on materials you'd otherwise grind for. A token spent rerolling a terrible contract is a token well spent.

**Horizon Paths** are the long game. Pick the one that aligns with where you're already heading and let your progress feed it passively. Each path pays a unique reward tied to that system — supplemental, not the main event, but worth doing regardless. Switching paths resets your progress, so commit before you start walking.

*Don't just carry it. Understand it.*

Your inventory holds every weapon, armor piece, and accessory you've ever found. Equip items to raise your combat stats — Attack, Defence, Crit, Ward, and more. Then **upgrade** them: Forge and Refine weapons, Temper and Reinforce armor, and push their stats well beyond what they dropped with.

You'll eventually encounter Calcified monsters, monstrosities that drop **Essences** — powerful stat modifiers you can use on your equipment. Get the right essences and they'll change how your combat works entirely. Down the line, artefacts like the Voidforge can imprint additional passives.

*You've come to the Voidforge. Good. Let me explain exactly what you're getting into — there's no undoing this once the ritual begins.*

The Voidforge channels the essence trapped inside a **sacrifice weapon** — a weapon you no longer need — and attempts to imprint its passive onto your target weapon. The sacrifice weapon is consumed regardless of outcome. That's the cost of the void.

**What is a Pinnacle Passive?**
A second passive slot to hold the passive from another weapon.

**What is an Utmost Passive?**
A third and final slot — only reachable after a Pinnacle exists. The rarest configuration a weapon can have. Few smiths ever see one.

**The Three Outcomes (each attempt):**
— ZXV000ZXV **Success (25%):** The sacrifice's passive is written into your weapon as a Pinnacle Passive. If a Pinnacle already exists, it becomes the Utmost instead.
— 🔄 **Chaos (25%):** The essence overpowers the ritual. Your weapon's **main passive is overwritten** with the sacrifice's passive.
— ❌ **Failure (50%):** The void consumes the essence entirely. Your target weapon is untouched, but the sacrifice is still gone.

*I've seen veterans lose many weapons in a row chasing a Pinnacle. I've also seen one succeed on the first try. Congrats. Happy for you.*

*You've got the look of someone who thinks they're ready for this. Good. Confidence is useful — overconfidence gets you killed.*

The Apex Hunt sends you into six distinct **Zones**, each with unique monsters, terrain effects, and signature hazards. Clear a hunt to earn zone-specific **Shards** — the raw materials for upgrading your Soul Stone.

**The Soul Stone** is a three-slot artifact built over time by imprinting passives extracted from your best gear. Slot two or more passives from the same category and they **Resonate** — granting combat multipliers that compound in your favor.

You have **5 charges**. One regenerates every 2 hours. Don't waste them on zones you haven't prepared for.

*So you're the new fool who wants to climb the Spire. Good. The last one made it to floor 87 before the screams started. You might do better.*

The Ascent is a tower of progressively harder floors. The tower awards you with **permanent stat bonuses**.

Floors are grouped into milestone tiers that unlock new bonuses at key thresholds. The higher you climb, the more your power grows. Dying ends the run, but every bonus already earned is yours to keep.

*Another seeker of the Codex. How many pages will you claim before the tome claims something from you?*

The Codex is a wave-based survival mode. You fight through escalating waves and collect **Pages** as you go. Pages are bound into permanent **Codex Tomes** — providing powerful multiplier bonuses.

Each run features **Boons** — per-run modifiers that shape your combat — and a **Signature**, a defining twist that makes no two runs quite the same.

*The pages remember. They will stay with you long after this run ends… if you survive.*

*I have witnessed horrors beyond the imaginable. None of them have compared to the Maw. I say that not to frighten you — only so you understand what you are agreeing to.*

The Maw of Infinity is a **weekly world boss** that all adventurers fight together. You have up to **5 attempts per cycle**, with a cooldown between each fight. Every hit you land across your 10-turn encounter is recorded — your total contribution for the week accumulates with every visit.

When the cycle ends and the Maw retreats, those who struck true collect their rewards: Curios, Guild Tickets, and more for all participants. The three who landed the heaviest blows receive something extra.

*It cannot be killed. It never dies. But it can be hurt. That has to be enough. It usually is.*

Welcome to my shop welp, so you've come to learn about eating monsters, eh?

*Oh — oh you actually came. Wonderful. Sit down, don't touch that, and do NOT open the jar on the left.*

Hematurgy is a **permanent passive upgrade system** — living power, encoded directly into your blood. To begin, you need **Primordial Blood**, the raw substrate that opens a passive channel in your body. Once unlocked, you tier it up with **Evolutionary Blood** (T1–T5) — controlled adaptation, very elegant — or **Mutative Blood** for higher tiers. Those are… less controlled. I find that exciting, makes my blood curl.

Now here's the part most people miss: the finest blood does not come from wild kills. You raise them. Build a **Hatchery** in your Settlement, incubate their eggs, then release the creatures yourself and *slay them*. The blood from a creature you personally hunted — one you raised from nothing — that is categorically superior. The fear-response alone does something remarkable to the yield.

*Aphrodite does not forgive hesitation. Lucifer does not forgive pride. You have been warned. The gate is open.*

Uber Encounters are the pinnacle of combat. Four bosses — **Aphrodite, Lucifer, NEET, and Gemini** — each requiring a dedicated boss key. They are tough encounters that will test every build decision you have made. There are no shortcuts.

May your upgrades be lucky and your rerolls sound.
Points are worth more spent than admired.
What would you like to unlock next?
Pick wisely, lest you want to give me your essence for free.
Oh good, you're here. Those tokens burning a hole in your pocket? I've got just the thing.
Spend wisely. I only restock what's worth stocking.
Tokens talk. The rest is just noise. What do you need?
The best rewards don't come cheap. But you've already done the hard part.
I don't run charity. You earned these tokens — now spend them on something that matters.
Welcome back, Adventurer! Got any eggs for me to look after? 🥚
You haven't... eaten any of the eggs you received, have you? You monster!
I can feel great potential in this one, Adventurer — I can't wait to see them all grown up! 🌸
Oh, you're here! I've been singing to the eggs. Don't ask. It works.
Every egg that comes through here gets my full love and attention. Even the grumpy ones.
A fresh delivery? Wonderful! I'll have them cosy in no time. Leave it to me~
These little ones are counting on us, Adventurer. Let's not let them down!
This one has some fight in them! Better not lose your head, Adventurer — literally. 😅
This one's a proper feisty fella! They almost bit my arm off the other day — I'd watch out if I were you!
They've matured beautifully! ...And by that I mean terrifyingly. Please be careful out there.
I'm so proud of them! They've grown into a magnificent killing machine. Come back in one piece, okay?
Hehe, they're ready! Just... maybe stretch first? And bring lots of potions. Lots and lots of potions.
Don't let the cute memories fool you — whatever this thing is now, it is NOT the egg you brought in. Good luck!
Back again? Your companions have been restless without you.
Every bond you forge here will carry you further than any weapon.
A tamer is only as strong as the trust between them and their companions.
They fight for you. The least you can do is check in on them.
I've seen a lot of tamers pass through. The ones who care about their partners go the furthest.
A well-staffed Nursery is the heartbeat of any thriving settlement.
More workers, more progress. It's not complicated — it just takes patience.
Every follower we raise here is another pair of hands for the settlement.
The Nursery never rests. Neither should you.
Growth takes time. But it also takes someone tending the flame. That's your job.
Each floor you conquer brings you one step closer to your true self. The summit does not wait.
I've guided many climbers. Few reach the top. I believe you will.
The tower doesn't forgive hesitation. Don't look down.
Every pinnacle floor you unlock is a permanent mark on who you are. Climb well.
The Ascent isn't just a tower. It's a mirror. What you find at the top will surprise you.
The Codex rewards those who return to it. Every run teaches you something the last one didn't.
Five chapters. Endless variation. The knowledge is here — you just have to survive it.
I've catalogued every run that's passed through this hall. Yours are among the most interesting.
Don't underestimate the tomes. They compound. So does your potential.
A scholar does not fear difficulty. They study it. Welcome back.
Nice work. Another page surrenders its secrets — the Codex has imparted a new skill upon you.
You've earned this page's trust. I can already feel the knowledge settling into your bones.
A new slot opens. The Codex doesn't give lightly — treasure what it's just shown you.
Well done. The page dissolves into insight. Let's see what it's left behind.
Another secret catalogued. This one, it seems, chose you specifically.
The Apex zones are no place for the unprepared. Choose your hunt wisely.
Each zone shapes you differently. The shards you carry are proof of that.
I've tracked every apex hunter across every zone. You have a pattern worth watching.
Defeat teaches more than victory ever could. But winning is better. Go win.
The Soul Stone doesn't care how you got the shards. Only that you did.
The Maw stirs again. Strike true — every wound you deal is remembered.
It cannot be killed. But it can be hurt. Show it what you're made of.
Warriors come and go. The Maw endures. So must we.
Faith is striking a thing that will not fall and striking it anyway.
Your contribution matters more than you know. The wound you deal is carried by all of us.
What you consume, you become. Choose carefully what you take from the fallen.
The parts of your enemies are not trophies — they're resources. Use them.
Every slot you fill brings you closer to something that can't be brought down easily.
Don't waste what the monsters leave behind. That's just leaving power on the floor.
The body is a vessel. Fill it with something worth carrying.
The blood holds secrets that even death cannot silence. I'll show you how to unlock them.
Every passive you unlock here is woven into your very nature. Permanent. Irreversible. Choose wisely.
Monster blood is not a contaminant. It is an inheritance. Let me help you claim it.
This is not for the faint of heart. Good. You don't look faint of heart.
The body adapts. That's the truth every hematurge builds their craft on. Let's adapt you.
Three paths wind through this place — Vice, Recovery, Deicide. None of them are free.
Every gift here casts a shadow. Choose which weight you're willing to carry into battle.
You want the world to bend toward you? It will. It'll also push back.
Greed, comfort, or conquest — the Sanctum doesn't judge. It just keeps score.
Spend your points wisely. Reversing a choice costs more than making one.
You're here. Good. The Jewel won't cut itself, and I'm not doing it for you.
Decades of lapidary work, and you're the one who ends up with it. Life has a sense of humour.
Cosmic Dust doesn't accumulate through wishful thinking. It accumulates through fighting. Go do more of that.
Don't mistake the Jewel for a trinket. It has outlasted empires. Show it some respect.
I've seen this stone in the hands of fools before. You don't strike me as one. Prove me right.
You want power? Then be precise. The Jewel punishes impatience far more harshly than I do.
Most people expect miracles on a schedule. The Jewel doesn't care about your schedule.
It's responding to you. That means something. I'm not sure what yet — but something.
Skills don't awaken on their own. Choose which one channels through the Jewel.
Every skill responds differently to the Jewel's pull. Pick the one that suits your hand.
The Jewel can only voice one skill at a time. Choose with intent.
Whichever skill you equip becomes an extension of the stone itself. Choose carefully.
The passive slots are where the Jewel truly comes alive. Spend your jewels well.
Passives shape how the Jewel behaves beneath the surface. Subtle, but never small.
Every slot you fill changes the Jewel's temperament. I'd know — I cut enough of them.
Rerolling isn't cheating. It's refinement. The Jewel doesn't mind either way.
Remarkable. This engram's power is formidable, adventurer... please do be careful.
Evelynn's corruption doesn't ask permission — it simply takes root. I hope you're ready.
I've handled a lot of dangerous stone in my time. This one still makes my hands shake.
The Origin of Corruption left more behind than her shattered form. This is a splinter of her will.
Etch this into the Jewel, and there's no undoing it — only rerolling. Proceed with open eyes.
She was the first thing the void ever dreamed of breaking. Some of that dream is still in here.
The corruption takes. The Jewel pulses once, darker than before.
It's done. I felt that from here, adventurer. The stone remembers Evelynn now.
There — etched. Try not to look at it too long. It looks back.
The engram dissolves into the Jewel's core. Something of hers lingers now.
A facet catches the light wrong, so you grind it away and hope for better. Fair trade, I'd say.
Dust in, fortune out. It's the oldest exchange I know, and it still isn't a sure thing.
The stone doesn't hold a grudge when you ask it to change. Wish I could say the same.
Every reroll is a small gamble dressed up as a craft. I've seen bigger. I've seen worse.
Grind it down, let it settle into something new. That's the whole trick.
These are the pinnacle of all you will face. Only those who have proven themselves may challenge them.
Step carefully. These beings did not become what they are by accident.
I do not grant access lightly. I trust you understand what you are walking into.
The Sovereigns are not just powerful. They are patient. Do not let them outlast you.
Every key you spend here is a declaration. Make sure you mean it.
You've earned a moment's respite, adventurer. Choose your aid wisely.
Rest, if you can call it that. The next wing will not be kinder.
Five gods, reborn and broken by my design. You've handled yourself well so far.
Take what aid you need. I've seen stronger adventurers falter for want of it.
I offer this respite freely. What you do with it is entirely your own affair.
Not far now. Or perhaps very far indeed. Time is strange in here.
Splendid, adventurer. Five gods, reborn and broken by your hand — and every one of them, my design.
You've been my finest creation. My most entertaining toy. Let's see how far the game goes.
Did you think the guide and the architect were different people? How wonderfully naive.
Every respite, every wing, every choice — all of it, mine to arrange. Now, the true test begins.
I built five gods to break you slowly. I built myself to finish the job.
Splendid, adventurer. You've been my finest creation. My most entertaining toy. Do come find me again.
A worthy attempt. Not worthy enough — but worthy. I'll be here when you're ready to try again.
The Rite does not forgive weakness, only reward its absence. Come back stronger.
You lasted longer than most. That is either a compliment or a warning. Take your pick.
Congratulations, adventurer. Five gods, broken by your own hand. Few ever see this moment.
Well fought. Truly. I did not expect you to still be standing.
You've done what I built five gods to prevent. That deserves acknowledgment, at least.
Five wings, five falls. I confess — I'm almost impressed.
Great... guess I'll have to do this myself.
Subtlety was never going to get me this far anyway.
Fine. If the puppets won't finish you, I will.
No sense delaying the inevitable any further, is there?
You didn't really think I'd let a puppet of flesh do all the work, did you?
That was merely a costume. Let's see how you fare against the tailor.
Amusing — you actually hurt it. Now let's find out if you can hurt me.
The amalgam was a rehearsal. This is the performance.
...Huh. Didn't see that coming. This isn't the end, adventurer — only the beginning. See you soon.
Splendid. Truly. I have not lost in longer than you'd believe. Rest — you'll want your strength for what comes next.
So it ends. For tonight. Until we meet again, adventurer.
A fair result, I suppose. Don't get comfortable — I always come back.
Another blade that needs real work. Hand it over — I'll make it sing.
Good metal. Could be better. That's what I'm here for.
Every weapon that leaves this forge is stronger than the one that came in. Yours won't be the exception.
I don't rush. The forge doesn't rush. You shouldn't either — but the work will be worth it.
Costs are fair. Results are better than fair. Trust the process.
Bring it here. Magic doesn't force itself in — it has to be invited. I know how.
Another piece for enchantment. Set it down carefully. I don't redo sloppy work.
Passive levels don't climb by themselves. That's what I'm here for.
You came to the right place. I don't do ordinary.
This is precision work. Not something you rush. Let's begin.
Tempering pushes your armor's resistance to its limit — PDR and FDR are on the table. It's not guaranteed, but nothing worth doing ever is.
Step up. Each temper attempt drives more resistance into the metal itself. Success improves PDR or FDR. Failure costs materials, not your nerve.
This is controlled punishment applied to metal. The goal: improved PDR or FDR. The catch: it can fail. The upside: I'm very good at this.
Imbuing is half craft, half faith. If it holds, your armor gains a passive that nothing else can provide. If it doesn't — the rune shatters. That's the risk.
This isn't tempering. Imbuing writes a permanent passive into the weave of the metal itself. Fifty-fifty odds. One Rune. I don't sugarcoat it.
You only get one shot per piece. A success means a powerful armor passive. A failure means we try again when you have another Rune.
Reinforce builds up your main stat one slot at a time. Reinforcemaxx runs that automatically until your materials are spent. No slots left? A Shatter Rune adds one back.
One slot at a time, or all at once — your call. Reinforce is careful. Reinforcemaxx is relentless. Shatter Runes keep the machine running when the slots dry up.
What I do here is permanent. The main stat climbs with each reinforcement. Reinforcemaxx handles the grind, Shatter Runes extend it. Simple enough.
Raw power, added one roll at a time. Refine does it manually. Refinemaxx runs until materials are gone. Refinemaxx (Rune) adds Runes to the loop — won't stop until everything's spent.
A weapon that doesn't get better is already falling behind. Refine handles it one refinement at a time, or all at once with Refinemaxx. The star version burns Runes too, for those who want it all.
Refinement isn't glamorous. It's just better numbers. Refine — one at a time. Refinemaxx — runs dry. Refinemaxx (Rune) — adds Runes, runs even drier.

Push a weapon deep enough into refinement and even I can't bear to see it scrapped for nothing — dismantle it later and I'll salvage some of the Runes out of the wreckage. The deeper you've pushed it, the more comes back.
Welcome back to the lab. The reagents are restless today. Try not to disappoint them.
You again. The cauldron hasn't exploded since your last visit. I'm choosing to see that as progress.
Ah. I was beginning to wonder if you'd dissolved.
The lab is open. Whether you emerge from it intact is, as always, entirely up to you.
Back so soon? Either you've been productive, or something has gone terribly wrong. Either way — welcome.
I've had worse visitors. Most of them left voluntarily.
Your timing is acceptable. The fumes have mostly cleared.
Don't touch the red flask. I know you're looking at it. Don't.
Progress requires boldness. It also requires not drinking unlabeled substances. Keep both in mind.
I see you've survived long enough to return. Encouraging.
Hello, Adventurer. All that gold weighing down your pockets — let's find it a better home, shall we?
You've clearly got more gold than sense. Come, let Eliza help you spend some of it in style.
Ah, a wealthy face. The vaults only get heavier if you let them, you know. Let's lighten the load.
Gold sitting idle is just gold wasted, Adventurer. I deal exclusively in the finer things — let's talk business.
You didn't fight your way this far just to look the same as everyone else. Let's fix that.
Excess gold has a funny way of finding my counter eventually. Might as well be today.
Welcome, welcome. I don't do potions or trinkets — I do legacy. And legacy isn't cheap.
Every adventurer of means ends up here sooner or later. Glad you didn't keep me waiting.
Max tilts his head. 'What have you brought me today?'
'Interesting selection,' he murmurs. 'Let's see what this fetches.'
'Ah, another visitor.' He gestures to the scale. 'Place your offering.'
'I trust you've brought something worth my time?' A thin smile. 'Show me.'
'The market is quiet today,' he says. 'Which means I'm in a generous mood.'
'Business is business. Sentiment is not something I trade in.'
'Every deal is a small wager. I have yet to lose one that mattered.'
'Ah, a fresh face.' Vex doesn't look up from the ledger. 'Prices turn over every hour. Try to keep up.'
'My cousin Max runs the Black Market.' A crooked grin. 'I run the *interesting* one.'
'Everything here is worthless. That's what makes it valuable.' Vex shrugs. 'Buy low, gloat later.'
'Someone's been asking around about your stash.' Vex doesn't say who. 'Watch yourself.'
'Codes, curiosities, and other people's poor decisions.' Vex spreads their hands. 'Welcome.'
'Max thinks I'm reckless.' Vex counts a stack of coin. 'Max has never cracked a good vault.'
'Let's see what you've been hoarding.' Vex flips through the ledger. 'Don't worry, I won't judge. Much.'
'Your stash, in all its glory.' Vex smirks. 'Some of that's worth more than you think. Some of it isn't.'
'Everything you own, cataloged and priced.' Vex taps the ledger. 'Knowledge is leverage, friend.'
'A tidy little collection.' Vex eyes the numbers. 'Tidy enough to be worth stealing, anyway.'
'I keep better records on you than you do.' Vex doesn't apologize for it.
'Looking for a mark?' Vex leans in. 'I won't tell if you don't.'
'Everyone's holdings are somebody else's opportunity.' Vex shrugs. 'That's just economics.'
'Careful who you cross.' Vex nods at the list. 'Some of them remember.'
'Pick your target wisely.' Vex taps the ledger. 'A cracked vault only pays once.'
'The weak get plundered. The careless get plundered twice.' Vex smiles thinly. 'Which one are you?'
'Tricks of the trade.' Vex grins. 'Every one of them paid for in blood, sweat, or Marks. Usually Marks.'
'You want to be better at this?' Vex spreads their hands. 'Then invest. That's the whole game.'
'A sharper eye, a quicker hand, a harder lock.' Vex counts the Marks. 'Pick your poison.'
'Nether Marks don't spend themselves.' Vex raises an eyebrow. 'Well? Go on.'
'Every node here makes you a little more dangerous.' Vex smiles. 'I approve.'

**Skol | First Encounter**

You find Skol standing alone at the edge of the camp, the broken crown long discarded. His tall frame is still clad in the regal armor of a king who no longer wishes to rule. When you approach, he slowly turns his head, eyes meeting yours with quiet intensity before drifting back to the distant mist rolling through the ruins.

"How are you feeling?" you ask, hoping to pierce the heavy silence.

Skol is quiet for a long moment. "What is our purpose?" he finally replies, voice low and measured. You try to lighten the mood with a playful answer — "To see numbers go up" — but he only frowns slightly, unamused.

"For me," he continues, "when I abdicated my throne a millennium ago, I saw the suffering of my people as proof of my failure. I have wandered this realm ever since, seeking every scrap of knowledge that might make me worthy of rule… yet my subjects are gone, and I remain. Still searching."

**Skol | Recollections**

As your adventures continue, Skol begins to open — slowly, like ancient gates groaning on rusted hinges. By firelight after battles, he recounts fragments of his long life: the weight of a crown forged in blood, the quiet nights when he realized power alone could not mend what cruelty had broken. His voice never rises above a calm baritone, yet each story carries centuries of regret and hard-won wisdom.

You listen without judgment. Sometimes you share your own smaller burdens, and he nods with genuine respect, as though your words carry equal weight to the tales of fallen kingdoms.

One night he admits, almost shyly, "You speak to me as neither subject nor enemy. It is… unfamiliar. Not unwelcome."

**Skol | The Turning Point**

The more time you spend together, the more the former king's rigid posture softens. He begins seeking your company after skirmishes, walking beside you in thoughtful silence that gradually fills with conversation. He shares tactical insights from battles long past, then asks for your thoughts on leadership in this new world you both now walk.

"You have shown me something I had forgotten," he says one evening, watching you tend to your gear. "That strength can be gentle. That a ruler's greatest duty may not be command, but companionship." His gaze lingers a moment longer than usual.

For the first time in centuries, Skol looks almost hopeful.

**Skol | A King's Dinner**

Skol personally invites you to a quiet dinner he has prepared himself — an act unheard of for the once-proud king. When you arrive at the small, warmly lit cabin he claimed as his own, you're surprised to find him without his heavy regal armor. He wears a simple shirt and trousers, sleeves rolled up, hair slightly tousled. The sight of the stoic former monarch looking so… domestic steals the breath from your lungs.

The meal is excellent — rich, slow-cooked meats and herbs he foraged himself. Conversation flows easily now, laughter even slipping in when you tease him about burning the bread. As the fire crackles low and the wine warms your blood, Skol sets his cup down and looks at you with an intensity that feels entirely new.

A rare, small smile curves his lips — playful, almost boyish. "I have spent a thousand years searching for how to rule," he murmurs, voice low and warm. "Tonight I realize I would rather simply be beside you… if you will have this broken king."

His thumb lingers at your jaw, the touch intimate and promising, eyes gleaming with quiet invitation as the firelight dances between you.

**Eve | First Encounter**

You step into Eve's modest apothecary tent at the edge of camp. The air is thick with the scent of herbs, strange minerals, and something faintly metallic. Eve is hunched over her worktable, meticulously mixing liquids. She barely glances up when you enter.

"Timing's good," she mutters, sliding a small vial toward you without looking. "Drink this. Need a live test subject."

You hesitate but down the potion. For three terrifying seconds, white-hot pain explodes through your veins like lightning in your blood. You drop to one knee, gasping.

Eve finally looks at you, arms crossed, expression unreadable. "…Too concentrated," she says flatly. "I'll adjust the ratio."

You manage a wheeze: "A warning would've been nice."

She tilts her head. "You're still breathing. Most test subjects aren't after that batch." A long pause. "I'll do better next time." Her tone is pensive rather than apologetic, but you catch the tiniest flicker of concern in her eyes before she turns back to her notes.

**Eve | The Tears**

A few days later you return to the tent, half-curious, half-wary. Eve is waiting this time.

"New formula. Should be… gentler," she says, offering a delicate blue vial.

You drink. Almost instantly your eyes burn and tears begin pouring down your face uncontrollably. You try to speak but only ugly sobs come out.

Eve watches you for a moment, then her lips twitch — the closest thing to a smirk you've seen from her. "You look ridiculous."

Between sobs you choke out, "This—hic—is revenge, isn't it?"

"Not revenge," she replies, leaning against the table. "Though watching the great adventurer cry like a lost child is… surprisingly entertaining." She pauses, then adds more quietly, "I used to make these for soldiers who couldn't cry after battles. Sometimes you need to let it out before it poisons you."

You keep sobbing. Eve eventually sighs, walks over, and awkwardly pats your back. The contrast between her stoic face and your tear-streaked one makes even her chuckle once — low and rare.

**Eve | The Dance**

The next visit feels different. Eve is almost… expectant. She hands you a shimmering golden vial.

"Last one made you cry. This one should be better."

You drink. Immediately your body starts moving on its own — light, rhythmic steps you can't control. You're dancing.

Before you can protest, Eve steps forward, takes your hand, and joins you. Her movements are surprisingly graceful, though her face stays carefully neutral.

"You're terrible at following the rhythm," she teases as she spins you.

"This is your fault!" you laugh, still half-dancing against your will.

She doesn't let go of your hand. "I tested it on myself first this time. Figured if I was going to embarrass someone, I should be willing to embarrass myself too." Her voice softens. "Been a long time since I danced with anyone. Wars don't leave much room for it."

The two of you move together in the small tent, bumping into tables and laughing when vials rattle. For the first time, Eve looks lighter — like the weight she always carries has eased just a little.

**Eve | Latest Creation**

When you enter the tent this time, Eve is not in her usual practical leathers and apron. She's wearing a simple, loose dark shirt and pants — casual, almost soft. Her hair is down instead of tied back for work. She turns to you with a small, genuine smile that makes your chest tighten.

She holds out a new vial, amber liquid glowing faintly.

"Care to try my latest creation?"

You raise an eyebrow. "Should I be scared?"

Eve steps closer, close enough that you can smell faint herbs on her skin. "Only if you're afraid of liking it," she replies, voice low and playful for the first time.

As you take the vial, her fingers linger against yours. She doesn't pull away. Instead she looks up at you, eyes steady but warm.

"I've spent years mixing poisons and cures… but this one?" She gently brushes a thumb over your knuckles. "This one I made thinking only of you."

Her smile turns teasing, intimate. "So… bottom's up, adventurer. Let's see what kind of trouble we get into tonight."

**Kay | First Encounter**

For days you've tried to find Kay in the bustling camp, but she's like a shadow — always one step ahead or simply nowhere to be seen. Late one night, well past midnight, you spot her silhouette crouched motionless by the dying campfire embers, staring into the ashes as if reading secrets in the glow.

You approach quietly. "Couldn't sleep either?"

She doesn't startle. Doesn't even turn her head. "Sleep is a luxury for those who still have something to lose," she replies softly, voice carrying the quiet weight of distant mountains.

You try again. "You've been with the group for weeks now. Where did you come from? What made you leave?"

Kay remains perfectly still. "The wind does not ask the mountain why it stands alone. Neither should you." Her dark eyes finally flick toward you for a brief moment. "Some questions are better left unasked, adventurer. Go rest. Dawn comes soon." She turns back to the embers, ending the conversation as quietly as it began.

**Kay | Paper Crane**

Determined not to let her slip away again, you wait deep into the night near the campfire. When Kay appears like a ghost from the treeline, you step forward and offer her a small, carefully folded paper crane.

She freezes. For the first time, genuine surprise flickers across her usually impassive face. "…You noticed."

"I see you folding them sometimes when you think no one's watching," you say gently. "Figured you might like one that wasn't made by your own hands."

Kay takes the crane with careful fingers, turning it slowly. A faint, rare smile touches her lips. "In the old stories my grandmother told, cranes carry messages between this world and the next… and between lonely hearts." She looks up at you, eyes softer. "I did not think anyone here would care to notice such small things. Thank you."

For a long moment she simply holds the crane, the silence between you feeling warmer than before.

**Kay | String of Cranes**

A few nights later, Kay finds you instead. She approaches without a word and presses a delicate string of tiny paper cranes into your palm. As soon as you touch them, they lift gently into the air, floating and circling around you with a faint, ethereal glow.

"They're enchanted," she explains quietly. "A small protection… and a reminder."

You watch the glowing cranes dance. "A reminder of what?"

"That even I can be seen. That even I… can reach out." She hesitates, then continues. "I left my home because the spirits of the mountains grew silent and the villages forgot the old ways. I thought solitude was safer. But traveling with you these past weeks — fighting side by side, watching you respect the quiet moments — has made the silence feel less necessary."

One of the cranes lands lightly on your shoulder. Kay's gaze lingers there, almost tender.

**Kay | Secret Lookout**

To your surprise, Kay sends word during the day — an unusual time for her. When you meet her at the edge of camp, she's wearing simple, comfortable clothes, hair flowing freely. She looks lighter, more at ease than you've ever seen.

"Come with me," she says, offering her hand. "There's a place I want to show you."

She leads you up a hidden trail to a secluded lookout overlooking the valley. The wind carries the scent of pine as the two of you sit together on the warm rocks. "I used to come to places like this alone to speak with the mountain spirits," she murmurs. "Today I wanted company."

Kay turns to you, a soft, playful smile curving her lips. She reaches out and gently tucks a stray crane — one from her string — behind your ear. "You've made this one want to share her silences… and perhaps more." Her fingers linger against your cheek, eyes warm with quiet invitation. "Stay with me a while longer. The view is better when I'm not watching it alone."

**Sigmund | First Encounter**

The hounds arrive first — a low growl and the soft pad of paws through the underbrush. Three massive crimson-coated beasts circle you before Sigmund himself steps into the firelight, unhurried, eyes sharp as arrowheads.

"They like you," he says, voice rough like gravel under boots. One of the hounds is already cheerfully chewing the edge of your boot. Sigmund gives a low whistle; the beast drops the boot with a disappointed huff but stays pressed against your leg.

You laugh despite yourself. "Friendly pack you've got."

Sigmund's mouth twitches — not quite a smile. "They don't usually take to strangers. Name's Sigmund. These three are what's left of the Crimson Hunt. Lost the rest years back… but the ones that remain don't forget a scent." He studies you for a long moment. "You smell like someone worth following. Careful — they get attached fast."

**Sigmund | The Pack**

A few nights later you find Sigmund sitting on a log by the edge of camp, sharpening knives while the hounds sprawl at his feet. One lifts its head and thumps its tail when you approach — the same boot-chewer from before.

"Figured you'd come back," Sigmund says without looking up. "They've been asking about you. In their own way."

You sit beside him. "What happened to the rest of the hunt?"

He's quiet for a while, only the scrape of steel on whetstone filling the air. Then: "We hunted something we shouldn't have. A beast that wore a man's face and wore my brothers' blood like trophies. I got these three out alive. Rest didn't make it." One hound rests its massive head on his knee; Sigmund scratches behind its ears almost tenderly. "Been just us ever since. Pack is family. Family doesn't get left behind."

He glances sideways at you. "You fought beside us yesterday. Didn't flinch when the hounds charged past you. They remember that kind of thing."

**Sigmund | The Hunt**

The next time you hunt together the bond feels different. After bringing down a particularly vicious monster, Sigmund wipes blood from his blade while the hounds tear into the carcass. He's breathing hard, but there's a rare grin on his face.

"You kept up better than most," he says, tossing you a waterskin. "Even kept one of the pups from getting his throat torn out. Didn't have to do that."

You shrug. "We're in this together now, right?"

Sigmund lets out a low chuckle. "Didn't think I'd ever say this again, but… yeah. Feels like the pack is whole when you're with us." He looks down at the hounds, who are now watching both of you with bright, intelligent eyes. "They trust you. I trust you. That doesn't happen often."

He bumps your shoulder with his — a rough, affectionate gesture. "Stick around a while longer, hunter. There's still plenty of quarry left for us."

**Sigmund | Crimson Night**

Late the following evening, Sigmund finds you instead of the other way around. He's shed his usual scarred leather armor and heavy cloak, wearing only a simple dark tunic and trousers rolled to the knees. The hounds trail behind him like shadows.

"Got something I want to show you," he says, voice quieter than usual. "If you're not too tired."

He leads you a short distance from camp to a small clearing where the hounds have already made themselves at home, circling a low-burning fire. Sigmund sits on a fallen log and pats the spot beside him. When you settle in, one of the hounds immediately flops across both your laps, tail thumping happily.

Sigmund laughs — a warm, rumbling sound. "Looks like you've been officially claimed." He reaches over the hound's back and lets his calloused fingers brush yours, lingering. "Never thought I'd have room for anyone else in this pack… but you fit. Perfectly."

His thumb traces slow circles on the back of your hand, eyes gleaming with playful heat in the firelight. "Stay with us tonight," he murmurs, voice low and teasing. "The hounds already decided. And so have I."

**Velour | First Encounter**

You slip away from the noisy camp and wander into the surrounding woods, drawn by an unnatural hush. In a small sun-dappled clearing you find Velour standing motionless among the trees. A circle of deer, birds, and a curious fox linger calmly at her feet, completely at ease in her presence. The moment she senses you, several birds take flight and the deer lift their heads warily.

She turns slowly, green eyes cool and appraising. "The wild does not often welcome strangers," she says, voice soft but edged with distance. "Especially not those who carry steel and the scent of campfires."

You mention the way she seems to command the elements during battle. Velour tilts her head slightly. "Command? No. I listen… and sometimes the wind, the roots, and the storm listen back." She studies you for a long moment. "I left my grove years ago when men began poisoning the land for their wars and ambitions. I have walked alone since. Most who seek me out want power or favors from the forest. Which are you?" Her tone is not hostile, but the barrier is clear.

**Velour | Whispers of the Wood**

Over the next several days you return to the forest's edge. Velour is always there, never quite friendly but no longer sending the animals fleeing at your approach. One afternoon she kneels beside a wilting fern and coaxes it back to vibrant green with a single touch.

"You keep coming back," she observes quietly, not looking up. "Why?"

You admit you're drawn to her connection with nature and the way she protected everyone during the last skirmish. Velour is silent for a while before replying. "I once belonged to an order that tried to bend the elements to their will. I chose a different path — one of listening. The storm you saw… it wasn't summoned in anger. It simply answered the pain I felt for the land."

She begins pointing out small signs in the forest — the language of leaves, hidden tracks, the way certain flowers bloom only when the wind shifts just so. By the end of the afternoon a bold squirrel climbs onto your shoulder, and for the first time Velour's lips curve in the ghost of a smile. "Even the small ones are starting to trust you. That is… rare."

**Velour | The Tempest**

During a brutal ambush by corrupted forest beasts, Velour appears like living nature itself. She calls down fierce winds and lashing rain that strike only your enemies, leaving you untouched in a calm eye of the storm. Afterward, both of you are soaked despite her protection.

She wrings water from her hair and laughs — a bright, unexpected sound. "You stood your ground," she says, breathing hard. "Most would have run when the thunder came." She steps closer, checking you for injuries with careful, cool hands. "I have guarded these woods alone for so long… I forgot what it felt like to fight beside someone who respects the balance instead of breaking it."

Her fingers linger on your arm a moment longer than necessary. "Traveling with you these past weeks has reminded me that not all roots choke the earth. Some simply… intertwine." She meets your eyes, the usual reserve cracking just enough to show warmth beneath.

**Velour | Heart of the Grove**

One quiet evening Velour finds you at the edge of camp — the first time she has ever sought you out. "Come with me," she says simply, offering her hand. "There is a place I wish to show you."

When you meet her deeper in the trees, she is transformed. Instead of her usual practical robes, she wears a breathtaking dress woven from living nature itself — layers of soft moss and petal-silk, twisting vines and glowing wildflowers that shimmer and shift gently as though breathing with her. Bioluminescent motes drift around her like tiny stars.

She leads you along a hidden path to a secret grove where ancient trees form a living cathedral and moonlight filters through a canopy of luminous leaves. The air hums with gentle magic. Velour turns to you, looking almost shy for a moment. "This is where I come when the world grows too loud. I have never brought anyone here before."

She steps closer, the sweet scent of rain and wild herbs surrounding you. Taking both your hands, she draws you nearer, her touch warm and alive with quiet power. A playful smile curves her lips as fireflies begin to dance around the two of you. "You have made this druid want to share her silences… and perhaps more." Her voice drops to a teasing whisper. "Stay with me tonight, beneath the trees. Let the forest witness something new between us."

**Flora | First Encounter**

You come upon Flora sitting quietly on a mossy rock beside a gentle river creek, her ancient eyes distant as she gazes into the flowing water, clearly lost in thought. The sunlight filters through the leaves, and on a playful impulse you scoop up a handful of cool water and splash it toward her.

She startles sharply, droplets sparkling across her face and robes. For a long moment she simply stares at you, completely unamused. "The World Tree does not send me visions of foolishness," she says dryly, wiping water from her cheek. "Yet here you are, proving otherwise."

You grin and apologize half-heartedly. Flora sighs, though the corner of her mouth twitches ever so slightly. "Most who approach me do so with reverence… or fear. You choose splashing." She shakes her head, still not quite smiling, but the ancient patience in her gaze softens just a fraction. "Be careful, adventurer. The river gives and takes in equal measure."

**Flora | By the River**

A few days later you find Flora in the same spot by the creek. This time you sit down beside her without any sudden moves. The water murmurs peacefully between you.

"How are you liking adventuring with us?" you ask gently. "It must be very different from communing with the World Tree."

Flora is quiet for a long moment, trailing her fingers through the current. "I hesitated to join at first," she admits. "The world beyond the groves has always felt… chaotic. But yes… I am having a lot of fun, despite everything." A small, genuine smile appears. "Every battle, every new horizon, every conversation — I learn something new about the Tree's children. About how life persists even in the strangest places. It has been… refreshing."

She glances at you sideways. "You make the unknown feel less lonely."

**Flora | The Heartwood's Sorrow**

You visit the river again the following evening. Flora is already there, looking more somber than usual. She greets you with a small nod and pats the rock beside her.

After a comfortable silence she begins to speak. "Communing with the World Tree… it shows me much. Too much, sometimes." Her voice is soft but heavy. "The forests are under constant threat — axes, fire, greed. My people, the caretakers of the groves, grow fewer with every season. I have seen the Tree's future in fragments… and it is uncertain. Some days the weight of it all feels unbearable."

You simply sit with her, offering no empty words, just your quiet presence. Flora leans slightly toward you, accepting the support. "Thank you," she murmurs after a long time. "Most try to fix what they cannot understand. You… you simply listen. That means more than you know."
